name: LVD
summary: A modular underground scintillator observatory at Gran Sasso monitors the Galaxy for neutrino bursts from stellar core collapse.
detection_principle: Hydrocarbon scintillator tanks detect prompt positron light and delayed neutron capture from inverse beta decay; timing across independent counters distinguishes bursts from backgrounds.

status.label: Operating / data taking
status.evidence: INFN Torino explicitly describes continuous operation since 1992 and the full configuration since 2001.

timeline.event: Continuous monitoring began with a partial detector.
Stellar-collapse burst monitoring continues in the institutional description.

collaboration.name: LVD Collaboration
lead_institutions: Institute for Nuclear Research, Russian Academy of Sciences
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Active target
key_parameters.value: Approximately 1,000 tonnes liquid scintillator at full configuration

key_parameters.name: Counter readout
key_parameters.value: Three photomultipliers view each approximately 1.5 m³ counter

results.summary: Developed online burst selection and long-duration Galactic-collapse monitoring; no new Galactic core-collapse burst is claimed in the cited apparatus and trigger sources.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
